name: Arizona
overview: Arizona sells tax lien certificates (Certificates of Purchase) on real property with delinquent property taxes, not the property itself. Each county treasurer runs one sale a year in February, and in the large counties it is held online through a third-party vendor (RealAuction's arizonataxsale.com sites). Bidders bid down the interest rate they will accept, starting at a 16% maximum, and the owner can redeem at any time by paying the taxes plus that interest. If the lien isn't redeemed, the holder must wait three years from the sale before starting a foreclosure action in court to get title.

counties.schedule_rule: The Online Tax Lien Sale will be open to the public each year in February for purchase of tax lien certificates.
counties.how_to_bid: The online sale opens about two weeks before the sale for viewing, new bidder registration and bidding on the Real Auction site. Bidders must be registered and have their initial deposit in by wire or ACH one day before the sale; the treasurer's office takes no deposits. The booklet says the deposit is $500 or 10% of the expected bid, whichever is greater, and the lien goes to the lowest interest-rate bid.
